project.descriptionEn: An immersive art-history gallery in the browser. Following the broad arc of Arts and Ideas, it threads twelve periods of art and more than ninety public-domain masterworks through a first-person 3D exhibition.

academicReference.noteEn: This project is intended for education and general interest. All explanatory text is original, written by the editors within an academic framework; it reproduces no passage from the source book.
coreTexts: Fleming, William & Marien, Mary Warner. Arts and Ideas. Thomson/Wadsworth, later editions.
Periodisation and narrative follow the ideologies, social conditions and prevailing spirit of the age that underlie artistic form.

licensing.policyEn: All images are drawn from Wikimedia Commons and are either in the public domain or released under CC0.
licensing.noticeEn: Dates and attributions have been compiled by this project; the licence on each file page is authoritative.
licensing.assetsEn: Images are used solely for local educational display and are packaged offline with the project.

network.networkEn: No external requests at runtime; all scripts, styles, fonts and images ship locally with dist.

ancient-medieval.descriptionEn: From cave images and Aegean and Roman wall painting to Byzantine mosaic and Gothic manuscript, art served above all cosmology, religious authority and the memory of a community.

early-renaissance.descriptionEn: Perspective, direct observation of nature and humanism arrived together. Painting turned from the icon toward a measurable world, and redefined humanity's place within it.

high-renaissance.descriptionEn: Leonardo, Raphael and Michelangelo fused the ideal body, classical order and scientific observation into a grand and highly synthesised vision.

baroque.descriptionEn: Reformation and Counter-Reformation recast what images were for. Theatrical light, dynamic composition and sensory intensity became a new language of persuasion and immersion.

rococo-neoclassicism.descriptionEn: Court taste turned toward refinement and pleasure, until the Enlightenment redirected art toward civic virtue, the ancient republic and rational grand narrative.

romanticism.descriptionEn: Industrialisation and an age of revolution placed individual feeling, historical trauma, the sublime in nature and national imagination at the centre of painting.

realism.descriptionEn: Courbet and the painters of Barbizon refused idealisation, carrying labour, city life and modern experience directly onto the canvas. Art became social observation.

impressionism.descriptionEn: The science of light and colour, the railway and leisured city life changed how people saw. Painters recorded the atmosphere of a moment and made the canvas a site of light.

post-impressionism.descriptionEn: Cézanne, Van Gogh, Gauguin and Seurat set out from Impressionism toward structure, emotion, symbol and scientific order respectively, heralding the independence of modern art.

modern-avant-garde.descriptionEn: Fauvism, Expressionism, abstraction and Suprematism declared the autonomy of form: colour, line and composition no longer imitated the world but created one.

expressionism-beyond.descriptionEn: War, the metropolis, the machine and spiritual anxiety drove painting toward distortion and violent colour, while the School of Paris redefined the modern figure through line and colour.

american-modern.nameEn: American Modernism and the Twentieth Century
american-modern.descriptionEn: American artists answered the industrial landscape with Precisionism, regionalist realism and abstract construction; postwar Abstract Expressionism and Pop continued these modern experiments.
